full_judgment:
Mahmudul Amin Chowdhury J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause why the judgment and order dated 17-10-96 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna in Miscellaneous case No.24 of 1995 should not be set aside. 

 2. The short fact leading to this Rule is, that the opposite party No.1 earlier instituted Title suit No.46 of 1994 before the Subordinate Judge, and Artha Rin Adalat No. 2. Khulna for closure and for realization of money by selling out the mortgaged property and in that suit the present petitioner entered appearance and filed written statement stating that he took loan and he has been making payment but he failed to make payment due to heavy loss in the brick business owing to flood. Then on 2- 11-1995 as the plaintiff took no steps the suit was dismissed for default. Thereafter the plaintiff opposite party No.1 instituted miscellaneous case No. 24 of 1995 under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat then by judgment dated 17-10-1996 allowed the Miscellaneous case and set aside the default order and restored the suit to its original file and number. The petitioner on being aggrieved by this order dated 17-10-1996 moved this court and obtained the present Rule. 

 4. Mr Md Nazrul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party Bank, on the other hand, submits that the provision of section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure is not available to a party in a proceeding under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain. He submits that the consistent view of the higher courts including Appellate Division is that a revisional application filed under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure is not available to a party aggrieved by any order passed by the Adalat and in support of his submission he placed reliance in the case of Sultana Jute Mills Ltd. and others vs Agrani Bank and others reported in 14 BLD (AD) 196 = 46 DLR (AD) 174. 

 5. It appears from the perusal of the available materials and from the submission made by the learned Advocates that the opposite party instituted Miscellaneous case No. 24 of 1995 under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code  of Civil Procedure praying for setting aside the order of dismissal of the suit which was earlier dismissed on default. It has been argued that the provision of Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure has no manner of application in a proceeding initiated before the Adalat under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain. It is well settled that the Artha Rin Adalat though a Civil court is a Court of defined nature having its own forum of appeal and in the Rin Adalat excepting the provision of Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure other provisions of the Code have not been made available. It a suit is dismissed for default the plaintiff may prefer an appeal but he cannot invoke the jurisdiction of the court under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure. It is well settled that the Rin Adalat is a self contained code having its own forum of appeal and in such a situation we hold that the Adalat has illegally assumed jurisdiction under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure and passed the impugned order dated 17-10-1996 and, as such, it requires interference. 

 8. Having given our anxious consideration to the materials on record and after hearing the learned Advocates of both the sides, we hold that the present application is not maintainable as the application under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not maintainable. We exercising our inherent power under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure set aside the order dated 17-10-1996 passed by the Adalat in the aforesaid suit and dismiss the aforesaid miscellaneous case.
